beats.say: Touching a butterfly's wings... won't *kill* it.
You catch one, see dust on your fingers... and *panic.*
Everyone says: now it can *never fly* again.
But that dust isn't dust. It's tiny *scales.*
Up to a *million* of them, stacked like roof tiles.
Butterflies lose a few scales on *every flight.*
Scientists even brushed the scales off monarchs... and they still *flew.*
Butterfly experts put it bluntly: the myth is *not true.*
Old butterflies flutter around *tattered* and faded... and keep going.
Still, scales matter. They make the *colors*...
...that attract a mate and warn off *birds.*
The real danger? Pinching the wing tips. They can *snap.*
So what *should* you do? Don't grab it at all.
Offer a finger, let it *climb on*, and carry it outside.
So next time you see that dust on your fingers... remember:
